scope: Flow-based detector for volumetric and scanning behavior. Not a general NIDS. Botnet, web attacks, infiltration, zero-day, and blocking are out of scope.

coverage_gate.reason: Families absent from at least one partition: DDoS, DoS GoldenEye, DoS Hulk, DoS Slowhttptest, DoS slowloris, PortScan. Validation and test positive families do not overlap.

half_split.rule: stable sort by Timestamp; first 50% of rows are train, the remainder is validation

expanding_folds.rule: stable sort by Timestamp; split into contiguous folds by row count; expanding-window CV fits earlier folds and validates on the next

decision.reason: The preregistered split cannot identify the supervised comparison: the training partition has no target positives, validation and test positive families are disjoint, and Wednesday's families are time-separated. A time-ordered amendment would be a family split.

options.name: Early/late Wednesday holdout
options.reason: Trains on slowloris/Slowhttptest and validates on Hulk/GoldenEye; DDoS/PortScan still have no training or validation rows.

options.name: Wednesday expanding-window CV with out-of-fold thresholds
options.reason: Uses all Wednesday rows for training and threshold selection, but the first fold has few positives and the test families remain unseen. The claim must be labelled cross-family zero-shot.

options.name: Unsupervised IsolationForest on Monday-Tuesday
options.reason: No positives are needed, but it cannot answer rules-vs-supervised and its Friday metrics are also zero-shot.

options.name: Move Wednesday into training
options.reason: Removes the validation partition and still leaves DDoS/PortScan test-only.

options.name: External volumetric/scanning data
options.reason: The only option that can provide positives in train and validation for the families that are tested. Requires data, licensing, and human approval.

notes: No model is trained, no registry row is written, and the serving artifact is untouched.
The family-day matrix uses the frozen partition label counts from the P2A and P2B audit artifacts.
The Wednesday time profile uses the frozen loader; raw and frozen row counts are both reported.
A time-ordered split is a family split because the CIC-IDS-2017 campaigns are sequential.
DDoS and PortScan appear only in the test partition, so their thresholds cannot be selected on Wednesday.
A1f and A2 are exploratory fallbacks; they do not satisfy the preregistered P2B mission.
findings: The training partition contains 0 primary volumetric/scanning positives. No supervised binary head can be fitted on Monday-Tuesday without changing the label policy or the split.

Validation positives are DoS GoldenEye, DoS Hulk, DoS Slowhttptest, DoS slowloris; test positives are DDoS, PortScan. The positive-family sets are disjoint: a threshold selected on Wednesday DoS traffic is applied zero-shot to Friday DDoS/PortScan.
Wednesday's primary families occupy disjoint time windows. A time-ordered split is therefore also a family split, not a representative sample of the target families.
A 50/50 time split trains on DoS Slowhttptest, DoS slowloris and validates on DoS GoldenEye, DoS Hulk, DoS Slowhttptest (11,167 train positives and 241,493 validation positives).
The first expanding-window fold contains only 5 primary positives (DoS slowloris), which is too small to train or calibrate a supervised model.
No threshold for DDoS or PortScan can be selected on Wednesday because those families do not appear there. Their test metrics are zero-shot descriptors, not validated operating points.

A1 as originally proposed (early Wednesday train, late Wednesday validation) is rejected as a primary P2B protocol. It is a cross-family zero-shot experiment and would not answer the requested comparison.
The proposed coverage gate fails for DDoS, DoS GoldenEye, DoS Hulk, DoS Slowhttptest, DoS slowloris, PortScan. No evaluated family is present in train, validation, and test.
